display.title: Episode 115: Life in the Hands of the Tongue, Chapter 1 (Adar)
display.summary_short: The Chofetz Chaim's lesson that words are like arrows, and the first chapter of the story of a hunter, a lion's milk and a dream in which the tongue claims to be king.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in Adar I 5744, a leap year with two months of Adar to grow in simchah before Purim. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor, a young guest leads the Shema in Studio 604. Story time opens with the Chofetz Chaim and his teaching of shmiras halashon: a person's life depends on his tongue. Like an arrow on a bowstring, words can still be chosen before we speak but cannot be called back once spoken, which is why Hashem guarded the tongue behind teeth and lips. The story: a beloved king falls gravely ill and can be cured only by lion's milk. A brave hunter takes ten goats, feeds the lion one each day until it trusts him, and fills a bucket with its milk. Resting on the way back, he dreams that his feet, hands, brain, eyes and ears each claim the reward, and when the tongue claims it too, they all laugh at it. The angry tongue vows to prove it is king of the body, to be continued. The mailbox brings a birthday request and a boy's wish that the show aired later. Uncle Yossi shares that most of his stories came from his late mother, whose yahrzeit is in Adar.
display.lesson: Think before you speak: once words leave your mouth you cannot call them back, so guard your tongue.

date.note: 'This year we have two Adars' and Purim is approaching (5744 was a leap year); a yahrzeit 'Beis Adar' is mentioned. Likely late Feb 1984.

sources_cited.note: The Baal Shem Tov: learn how to serve Hashem from everything you see or hear.
'Our Sages tell us' Hashem guarded the tongue with two walls, the teeth and the lips.
The story of the lion's milk and the quarreling limbs is 'told by our Sages' (no reference given).
